page: Microsoft Azure E32-8s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with constrained vCPU capacity within the ESv5 series. It runs on Microsoft Hyper-V and is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is allocated 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptographic instruction extensions including AVX-512, VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI.

A key characteristic of this configuration is its high memory-to-compute ratio, supplying 256.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 32.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, requiring attached remote storage for filesystem needs. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance delivers mid-tier compute results, producing a Geekbench multi-core score of 6200.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 11439.16. Memory bandwidth reaches 60.25 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 43.28 GB/sec for writes, sustaining 8.06 million Redis SET operations per second.

Due to the reduced vCPU allotment relative to memory size, workloads requiring extensive parallel multi-threading, such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression or larger LLM token generation, exhibit lower relative throughput. However, the architecture offers strong cost efficiency for software environments bound by per-core licensing models that still demand massive memory residency. Primary suitable workloads include enterprise relational databases, large in-memory caching platforms, and data analytics engines.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-8s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, paired with 256.0 GB of RAM. Designed with a constrained vCPU profile yielding 32.0 GB of memory per vCPU, it suits systems requiring substantial memory capacity without high core counts. The instance includes AVX-512 vector support, no local storage, and no GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, it achieves average single- and multi-core processing performance, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 11439.16 and Geekbench multi-core score of 6200.0, alongside 8.06 million Redis SET operations per second. While parallel CPU scaling is restricted by the 8 vCPU limit, the high RAM allocation provides a cost-effective operational profile for memory-heavy database engines, in-memory caches, and workloads with per-core software licensing constraints.
